text: A family who asked for a visit online is waiting to hear from us. An empty New list means nobody is waiting.
Online requests land in New. When you've worked one, it moves to Contacted, Booked or Not Booked.
The one thing to remember: every request ends as Booked or Not booked, with a reason. New should be empty at the end of the day.
The card shows who, which pet, why, and how soon.
And anything the family told us about timing.
The full form is one click away.
To book it, click Book.
Routing opens with the request filled in.
Pick the doctor and search, like any booking.
Use the family's note: mornings, not Wednesdays.
Book.
The pet and the visit type carry over. Check them.
Book appointment.
Scout brings you back to Appointments with a text to the family ready, arrival window filled in.
Send it, or cancel if you'd rather call. Scout checks before it drops the text.
Maple's request moved to Booked by itself.

One exception: if you book a request as a HOLD type, for example to keep a time while the family decides, it doesn't go to Booked. It shows On hold, and you follow it up on the Holds board, under Scheduling, Holds.
If a request can't be booked, click Not booked.
Pick the real reason. These feed our reports on why requests don't book.
Mark not booked.
Called and left a message? Mark contacted instead, and add a note, so the next person knows.

The most common mistakes: booking the visit from the calendar and leaving the request sitting in New, and Not booked with no real reason. Remember: every request ends as Booked or Not booked, with a reason. New should be empty at the end of the day.
